subject: MSA + Order Form — SLA redlines and maintenance window coordination
messages:
From: Alicia Gomez <agomez@zephyrus.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@zephyrus.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Jul 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: MSA/Order form: SLA redlines and maintenance window request

Hi Laura,

Thanks for the MSA + order form — we've gone through the SLA section with our ops and procurement teams and attached a redline (Zephyrus_Redlines_SLA.pdf) that captures our ask. High-level items: 

- Uptime target: we asked for 99.99% for production (your draft lists 99.95%). Our SRE team is insisting on the higher bar for our external customers.
- Service credits: remove the single-incident cap; we propose a rolling monthly credit equal to 10% of the monthly invoice per downtime tier, with an overall cap of two months' fees.
- P1/P2 response times: we requested P1 initial acknowledgement <= 30 minutes and mitigation plan within 2 hours.
- Maintenance windows: we want scheduled maintenance restricted to a 3-hour monthly window, ideally Sundays 01:00–04:00 UTC.
- Notice: 72-hour advance notice for non-emergency maintenance and a 24-hour SLA for emergency maintenance notifications.

Procurement timeline: we need to get to an agreed commercial redline and send to legal by 6 Aug; contract execution target is 20 Aug. Can you confirm who's handling legal on your side and whether Redwood can live with the maintenance/credits state above?

Attachments: Zephyrus_Redlines_SLA.pdf (redline, annotated)

Thanks,
Alicia Gomez
Head of Procurement, Zephyrus Analytics
Alicia Gomez | agomez@zephyrus.com | +1 415-555-0193

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Gomez <agomez@zephyrus.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Jul 2026 17:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA/Order form: SLA redlines and maintenance window request

Alicia — thanks for the clear redlines and timeline. We're aligned on the urgency. Looping in Hannah (legal) and Aditya (product/ops) to weigh in on the technical and legal trade-offs.

Quick, pragmatic responses to your bullets below:

- Uptime target: 99.95% is what we guarantee for hosted customers today. For Dedicated reserved pools we can discuss a 99.98% commitment (requires capacity reservation plus a small premium). Can you confirm if Zephyrus will be using Redwood Dedicated or Hosted?

- Service credits: we understand the ask to remove the single-incident cap. Our standard is a per-month credit schedule with a cap tied to the monthly invoice; we can move to the structure you proposed (10% per tier, monthly rolling) but need to propose a hard overall cap (we recommend two months' fees as a middle ground).

- Response times: P1 ack 1 hour / mitigation plan within 4 hours is our current target. Shortening ack to 30 minutes is operationally feasible only with an elevated support tier (we can offer that as an add-on).

- Maintenance windows: we are comfortable with a single 3-hour monthly window. Our ops preference is Monday 02:00–05:00 UTC to reduce impact across US and EU customers, but Sunday 01:00–04:00 UTC is workable if that's important to Zephyrus.

- Notice: 72-hour for routine maintenance is fine. For emergency maintenance we typically post notice as soon as practicable; committing to a 24–48 hour guaranteed notice window for every emergency will be difficult. Hannah, can you propose language that balances regulatory needs with our ability to react to critical incidents?

Next steps: Hannah, please review the Zephyrus redline and draft a tracked-change counter (attach to this thread). Aditya — can you confirm operational feasibility of the shorter P1 ack for a premium support add-on and the Dedicated 99.98% SLA? Alicia — once we have a single consolidated Redwood counterproof we can share via Drive and route a DocuSign link for signature.

Also FYI Alicia — here's the HubSpot deal: https://hubspot.example/deal/12345 so we stay coordinated on milestones.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Head of Commercial, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com | +1 650-555-0122

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Gomez <agomez@zephyrus.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Jul 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA/Order form: SLA redlines and maintenance window request

Hi all — I reviewed Zephyrus_Redlines_SLA.pdf and added a counters with tracked changes (see attached: Redwood_SLA_counter_v1.pdf). Top legal/contract points from our side: 

1) Uptime and measurement: propose explicit measurement window and uptime calculation that excludes Scheduled Maintenance (we will define Scheduled Maintenance as the mutually agreed monthly 3-hour window). We can offer 99.98% for Dedicated with a defined capacity reservation clause; for Hosted we must keep 99.95% language.

2) Service credits: we can accept a multi-tier monthly credit schedule similar to Zephyrus' structure but need a clear maximum liability clause (we're proposing "aggregate cap equal to two months' fees in any 12-month period"). This keeps the commercial compromise while protecting service stability.

3) Response SLAs: legal is okay with operational P1 ack/mitigation commitments so long as the Order Form lists an elevated support add-on that Zephyrus may select for the faster ack times. We will include a definition for "acknowledgement" and "mitigation plan" to avoid ambiguity.

4) Maintenance/notice: propose routine maintenance notice >=72 hours. For emergency maintenance we will commit to "reasonable notice" language and an obligation to notify customers as soon as practicable; we cannot guarantee notice before every emergency change (this is operationally infeasible). However, we're open to adding a clause that Redwood will not perform emergency maintenance unless it is strictly necessary for security or stability and will provide post-event reporting within 24 hours.

5) Evidence/evidence requests: Zephyrus asked for SOC 2 and runbooks — we'll attach a redacted SOC 2 summary and a brief runbook excerpt as part of the procurement pack.

I attached the counters (Redwood_SLA_counter_v1.pdf) with alternate language for the force majeure/emergency carveouts. Please review and let me know if Zephyrus can accept the add-on for accelerated P1 acknowledgements. If not, we'll need to bake in stronger indemnities for credit exposure.

Attachments: Redwood_SLA_counter_v1.pdf

Regards,
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
hannah.schmitt@redwood.com

From: Alicia Gomez <agomez@zephyrus.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Jul 2026 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA/Order form: SLA redlines and maintenance window request

Laura / Hannah / Aditya — thanks for the quick follow-up and for the counters. We're generally comfortable with the Dedicated vs Hosted distinction; Zephyrus intends to run production workloads on Redwood Dedicated (we'll need the 99.98% option). Two quick items before we proceed to signatures: 

1) Emergency maintenance notice: Zephyrus needs a commitment to provide as much notice as possible and a retroactive explanation within 24 hours. We can accept the "post-event reporting" approach, but we'd like the language to require a good-faith effort to notify stakeholders at least 48 hours before the maintenance when practicable. Can Hannah propose a sentence that captures this compromise?

2) Consolidated redline: can Redwood send a single consolidated counter with tracked changes and the intended DocuSign packet (MSA + Order Form + Annex A (SLA))? Procurement will aim to sign within two weeks after we receive the consolidated counter.

Attachments referenced: Zephyrus_Redlines_SLA.pdf (we re-attached our annotated copy for convenience)

If you can get the consolidated counter to us by COB Mon, 26 Jul, we can meet the internal legal review and stay on the 20 Aug execution target.

Best regards,
Alicia Gomez
Head of Procurement, Zephyrus Analytics
agomez@zephyrus.com | +1 415-555-0193
